papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptome analyses unveil that MYH11 links stemness to immunotherapy resistance in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Immunotherapy is an essential treatment strategy for lung cancer, yet resistance to it is often unavoidable, resulting in treatment failure and poor prognosis. The cancer stem cell (CSC) theory offers a valuable perspective for understanding tumor metastasis and resistance to immunotherapy. However, there is a scarcity of multi-omics studies that identify tumor stemness subpopulations and their associated signaling pathways. In this study, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with spatial transcriptomics sequencing (ST-seq) to identify a myosin heavy chain 11 (MYH11)-high stemnes
papers.summary: Combining single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, the authors identify a MYH11-high cancer stem cell subpopulation in non-small cell lung cancer that is linked to immunotherapy resistance. The study proposes MYH11 as a marker connecting tumor stemness to immune evasion, suggesting a potential target for overcoming treatment resistance.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals PDIA6 as a tumor-intrinsic driver of mesenchymal plasticity and vascular microenvironment remodeling in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by pronounced microenvironmental heterogeneity, severe hypoxia, and profound resistance to conventional and targeted therapies. While abnormal tumor angiogenesis and perivascular niches are recognized hallmarks of GBM, the tumor-intrinsic drivers that actively orchestrate malignant-endothelial crosstalk and structure protective vascular sanctuaries remain to be fully defined. To identify key tumor-intrinsic vascular orchestrators, this study focused on PDIA6 and investigated its functional role and clinical significance in GBM mesenchymal plasticity, maligna
papers.summary: Using spatial transcriptomics, this study identifies PDIA6 as a tumor-intrinsic driver in glioblastoma that promotes mesenchymal plasticity and remodels the vascular microenvironment, helping create protective perivascular niches. The findings link PDIA6 to malignant-endothelial crosstalk and suggest it contributes to therapy resistance, highlighting it as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence contributes to tumor progression and shapes the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet its prognostic and biological significance in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify senescence-associated prognostic signals through pan-cancer screening and to develop an integrated risk stratification framework for BLCA that bridges molecular characterization with translational relevance.
papers.summary: This study identifies cellular senescence-associated prognostic signals in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) through pan-cancer screening and builds an integrated risk stratification model that links molecular features to the tumor microenvironment. The work aims to bridge multi-omics characterization with translational relevance for BLCA prognosis.

papers.title: Lineage-mixed neurodevelopmental programs in pediatric sarcomas nominate tumor-selective surface antigen pairs.
papers.abstract: Pediatric solid tumors have low mutational burden, frequent oncogenic gene fusions, and developmental origins in arrested progenitor cells. Single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) could represent an ideal tool to assess whether these convergent biological features yield shared therapeutic vulnerabilities. However, while existing tools can extract gene expression programs for pan-tumor single-cell data, interpreting them requires domain expertise across many disciplines and diseases. Here, we analyzed a pan-pediatric scRNA-seq atlas of 266 patient-and xenograft-derived samples across 22 pediatric solid
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors analyzed a large single-cell RNA-seq atlas of 266 pediatric solid tumor samples and xenografts, finding that these tumors express mixed lineage neurodevelopmental gene programs reflecting arrested progenitor states. This lineage mixing nominates tumor-selective pairs of surface antigens that could serve as dual-targeting therapeutic vulnerabilities. The work demonstrates how pan-tumor single-cell atlases can reveal shared developmental dependencies across pediatric cancers.

papers.title: HOMED enables hierarchical and multimodal optimization of DNA methylation deconvolution across tissues.
papers.abstract: Cellular heterogeneity is a major confounder in bulk DNA methylation data used in epigenome-wide association studies. Existing reference-based DNAm deconvolution methods often overlook hierarchical relationships among related cell types and may generalize poorly across datasets due to limited variability in reference profiles. We developed HOMED (Hierarchically Optimized Methylation Deconvolution), a framework that integrates cell-type hierarchy, single-cell RNA sequencing-guided deconvolution, and paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data for CpG signature optimization. Across multiple simulated and real
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: HOMED is a new computational framework for DNA methylation deconvolution that accounts for hierarchical relationships among related cell types and uses single-cell RNA-seq plus paired bulk RNA-seq/DNAm data to optimize CpG signatures. This improves estimation of cell-type proportions in bulk methylation data across tissues, addressing a key confounder in epigenome-wide association studies.

papers.title: Categorization and analysis of 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency from single-cell RNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: Inferring hidden cellular dynamics from static single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data remains a critical challenge. Beyond pseudotime trajectories and RNA velocities, cell potency provides another perspective by estimating cellular differentiation potential from gene expression levels. We review 16 computational methods that define cell potency under different, sometimes contrasting, assumptions. On the basis of how they summarize gene expression into a potency measure, we categorize them into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based methods. Using a unified set of mathematical n
papers.summary: This review categorizes 16 computational methods for estimating cell potency (differentiation potential) from static scRNA-seq data into average-based, entropy-based, and knowledge-based approaches. The authors show these methods rest on different, sometimes conflicting assumptions, and provide a unified mathematical framework for comparing them. The work helps researchers choose appropriate potency-estimation tools and understand their limitations.

papers.title: CellMarker 3.0: an updated resource of manually curated and computationally predicted cell markers in human/mouse and interactive web tools for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.abstract: The updated CellMarker 3.0 resource (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/CellMarker) offers a comprehensive resource, integrating experimentally validated and robustly algorithm-predicted marker genes for diverse cell types across human and mouse tissues. In addition, web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data are described. CellMarker 3.0 was updated with more data and new features, including (i) appending 274 tissues, 1877 cell types, 64 040 markers, and 1 245 923 tissue-cell type-marker entries over the previous version. The current release con
papers.summary: CellMarker 3.0 is an updated database that curates experimentally validated cell-type marker genes for human and mouse tissues, now supplemented with computationally predicted markers. The release adds 274 tissues, 1,877 cell types, 64,040 markers, and over 1.2 million tissue-cell type-marker entries, and introduces interactive web tools for analyzing single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics data.

papers.title: A droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing method for the high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within individual cells.
papers.abstract: Recently, long-read sequencing methods have revolutionized genomic research by allowing the resolution of previously inaccessible regions across the genome. However, the throughput and scalability of these methods have hindered their general application in the field. To address this limitation, we developed droplet-based methods for the single-cell profiling of chromatin accessibility (droplet-based single-cell Nanopore ATAC-seq, dscNanoATAC) and histone modifications (droplet-based single-cell NanoCUT&Tag, dscNanoCUT) by combining a commercial microfluidic device and long-read sequencing plat
papers.summary: The authors developed droplet-based long-read single-cell epigenome sequencing methods, dscNanoATAC and dscNanoCUT, by combining a commercial microfluidic device with nanopore sequencing to profile chromatin accessibility and histone modifications in individual cells. This addresses the throughput and scalability limitations of prior long-read single-cell approaches, enabling high-throughput profiling of multidimensional regulatory elements within single cells.

papers.title: Overlapping yet distinct spatiomolecular profiles across mood disorders and biological sex in the human prefrontal cortex.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) and bipolar disorder (BD) exhibit both overlapping and distinct clinical features, including sex differences in prevalence and symptomatology, but how these similarities and differences are reflected at the molecular and cellular level in the human brain remains poorly understood. Here, we applied spatial transcriptomics to the human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex from individuals with MDD, BD, and neurotypical controls to resolve molecular programs associated with diagnosis and biological sex. Our analysis revealed sex- and diagnosis-specific differences across
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study used spatial transcriptomics to profile the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of individuals with major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, and neurotypical controls, revealing both overlapping and distinct molecular programs associated with diagnosis and biological sex. The findings show that mood disorders share some spatiomolecular features while also exhibiting diagnosis- and sex-specific differences in gene expression across cortical regions.

papers.title: Overcoming segmentation bottlenecks in brain tissue for spatial proteomic inference at population scale.
papers.abstract: In spatial proteomics across large cohorts, downstream estimates from tens of thousands of images depend on accurate cell segmentation. Yet pretrained segmentation models struggle with morphologically complex cell bodies in human brain tissue, and how domain adaptation affects downstream discovery remains unclear. Here, we introduce SPInfer, a workflow for spatial proteomic inference developed using 5,832 manually annotated cell bodies from 120 immunofluorescence images of the human prefrontal cortex. After benchmarking eight segmentation methods spanning classical, convolutional, and foundati
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present SPInfer, a workflow for spatial proteomic inference that addresses the challenge of accurate cell segmentation in morphologically complex human brain tissue. Using 5,832 manually annotated cell bodies from 120 immunofluorescence images of the prefrontal cortex, they benchmark eight segmentation methods and show how domain adaptation affects downstream discovery at population scale. This work provides a practical solution for large-cohort spatial proteomics studies where segmentation quality is critical.

papers.title: spaTransfer: transfer learning for single-cell and spatial transcriptomics data using non-negative matrix factorization.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in spatially-resolved transcriptomics have enabled profiling of gene expression in a spatial context, which has led to the generation of large-scale single-cell and spatial atlases with computationally-derived cell type or spatial domain labels. An increasingly important task with these data has become the transfer of cell type or spatial domain annotations from a given reference (or source) atlas into a new target tissue or sample. The reference and target datasets could be at different resolutions or measured on different experimental platforms. Here, we present a method to p
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: spaTransfer is a new computational method that uses non-negative matrix factorization to transfer cell type and spatial domain annotations from a reference single-cell or spatial transcriptomics atlas to new target samples. It is designed to handle references and targets that differ in resolution or were measured on different experimental platforms, addressing a key challenge in leveraging large-scale atlases.

papers.title: Denoising single-cell ATAC-seq data with Shannon entropy.
papers.abstract: Single-cell Assay for Transposase Accessible Chromatin with sequencing (scATAC-seq) is widely used to investigate chromatin accessibility but experiments often contain empty droplets, droplets containing damaged nuclei or cellular-debris. Accurately filtering high-quality nuclei is important as noisy droplets contribute reads that can distort downstream analysis and obscure rare cell population. Current approaches often rely on read depth and or predefined genomic features that are not exactly the same as chromatin accessibility landscape. Here, we present a Shannon entropy-based method that f
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce a Shannon entropy-based method for filtering low-quality and empty droplets in single-cell ATAC-seq data. By using entropy as a measure of signal complexity rather than relying on read depth or predefined genomic features, the approach aims to better distinguish genuine nuclei from noisy droplets that can distort downstream analyses and mask rare cell populations.

papers.title: CellWHISPER disentangles direct cell-cell communication from structural proximity.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics makes it possible to infer direct, contact-dependent cellular communication, but existing tools are prone to high error rates due to spatial structure in cell types and gene expression. We present CellWHISPER, a framework for inferring contact-mediated communication, including gap junctions and ligand-receptor signaling, from spatial transcriptomics data. CellWHISPER controls errors with a statistical procedure that accounts for confounding effects of cell-type-specific expression and spatial organization. Closed-form significance scores enable analysis of large data. A
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CellWHISPER is a new computational framework for inferring direct, contact-dependent cell-cell communication (gap junctions and ligand-receptor signaling) from spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses a key problem in existing tools—high false-positive rates caused by confounding from cell-type-specific expression and spatial organization—by using a statistical procedure that controls for these effects and provides closed-form significance scores, enabling analysis of large datasets.

papers.title: Spatial proximity to AD pathology defines cell-type and genotype-specific characteristics in human AD hippocampus.
papers.abstract: How amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques and tau phosphorylation spatially relate to cell response and genetic variation in Alzheimer's disease (AD) brain is currently unclear. We established a pipeline to concurrently annotate Aβ and AT8 ptau pathology and cell-specific MERFISH expression profiles in human control and AD hippocampus. We characterized expression signatures in glia and neurons proximal or distal to Aβ plaques, AT8 ptau-enriched neurons, or Aβ and AT8 ptau in combination, and used spatially-defined transcriptional signatures to infer pathology-associated states in large snRNA-seq datasets lac
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study developed a spatial transcriptomics pipeline combining MERFISH with concurrent annotation of amyloid-β plaques and AT8 phosphorylated tau in human control and Alzheimer's disease hippocampus. They identified cell-type-specific expression signatures in glia and neurons based on proximity to Aβ plaques, ptau-enriched neurons, or both pathologies together, and used these spatially defined signatures to infer pathology-associated states in large snRNA-seq datasets. The work links spatial proximity to AD pathology with cell-type and genotype-specific transcriptional responses.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Quality Control Reshapes Spatially Resolved Metabolic Flux Predictions in Prostate Cancer.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables region-resolved investigation of tumor metabolism, yet translating gene expression into reliable metabolic flux predictions remains challenging because genome-scale models can admit thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs). Here, we integrated spatial transcriptomic data from twelve annotated regions of a single prostate tumor, spanning normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3 and 3+4 tissues, with Human-GEM using an E-Flux framework incorporating defined nutrient constraints, explicit cycle certification, and loopless flux variability analysis. An initial naïve impl
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors integrated spatial transcriptomics from twelve annotated regions of a prostate tumor with the Human-GEM metabolic model using an E-Flux framework, adding nutrient constraints and explicit thermodynamic cycle certification. They show that removing thermodynamically infeasible cycles (TICs) via loopless flux variability analysis substantially reshapes spatially resolved metabolic flux predictions across normal, inflamed, and Gleason 3+3/3+4 regions. The work demonstrates that thermodynamic quality control is essential for reliable spatial flux inference in cancer metabolism.

papers.title: X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement.
papers.abstract: Targeted spatial transcriptomics platforms such as 10x Genomics Xenium measure a predefined panel of genes. A gene is usually detected in fewer cells in the spatial assay than in the single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) reference used to choose it, by an amount that differs from gene to gene. We present eXtensible Spatial Panel Evaluation And Refinement (X- SPEAR), a framework for designing and checking Xenium gene panels. Its marker-selection method, Decision-rule Aggregation for Rare-cell Typing (DART), learns short Boolean gene rules and keeps several gene-disjoint rules per cell type. DA
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: X-SPEAR is a framework for designing and evaluating targeted spatial transcriptomics gene panels (e.g., 10x Xenium), addressing the problem that genes detected in scRNA-seq references are often detected in fewer cells in the spatial assay, with gene-specific dropout. Its DART marker-selection method learns short Boolean gene rules and retains multiple gene-disjoint rules per cell type to improve rare-cell typing robustness.

papers.title: Survival-associated cellular communication networks in human solid cancers.
papers.abstract: Single-cell atlases have enabled the prediction of human cell-cell communication (CCC) networks in cancer, but whether predicted communication networks have clinical significance is not well understood. Here, we integrated a pan-solid cancer scRNA-seq atlas comprising 78 cell types from 318,426 quality-controlled cells with bulk RNA-seq and clinical outcome data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) to develop Single-cell-based Kaplan-Meier Analysis Network (SKyNet). SKyNet prioritizes ligand-receptor interactions associated with overall survival across 11 human solid cancers, predicting unique
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed SKyNet, a method that integrates single-cell RNA-seq cell-cell communication predictions with bulk RNA-seq and clinical survival data from TCGA across 11 solid cancers. By linking predicted ligand-receptor interactions to overall survival, SKyNet identifies cancer-type-specific communication networks associated with patient outcomes, suggesting that computationally inferred cell-cell communication has clinical relevance.

papers.title: Detection of Supporting-Cell-Associated Gene Transcripts in Adult Human Cochlear Tissue from Cadaveric Temporal Bones.
papers.abstract: The adult human cochlea is difficult to study because viable inner-ear tissue is rarely available and postmortem samples are technically challenging to process. Supporting cells are essential for cochlear architecture, ionic and osmotic balance, synaptic stability, stress responses, and potential regenerative signaling. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the feasibility of detecting transcripts associated with cochlear supporting-cell biology in adult human cadaveric cochlear tissue.
papers.summary: This study tested whether gene transcripts related to cochlear supporting cells can be detected in adult human cochlear tissue obtained from cadaveric temporal bones. The authors demonstrate feasibility of transcript detection in this hard-to-obtain tissue, which could enable future studies of supporting-cell biology in the adult human inner ear.

papers.title: PathwayFinder enables linked exploration of cell types and gene modules in spatially resolved transcriptomics data.
papers.abstract: The rapid development of spatially resolved transcriptomics technologies has provided opportunities and challenges for understanding biological systems. Interpreting these data requires integrated analysis of gene expression and cell types within their spatial context, however, existing tools fall short in scaling this linked interactive exploration to large-scale datasets. We present PathwayFinder, a visual analytics application designed to bridge the gap between gene-centric and cell-centric analysis. Unlike standard workflows that view cells and genes in isolation, PathwayFinder links them
papers.summary: PathwayFinder is a visual analytics tool for spatially resolved transcriptomics that links gene-centric and cell-centric views, allowing users to interactively explore gene modules and cell types together in their spatial context. It addresses the scalability limitations of existing tools for large datasets, enabling integrated analysis rather than viewing cells and genes in isolation.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of ge
papers.summary: PIANO is a deep learning framework that uses a generative model of gene expression to integrate single-cell multi-omics data. It addresses three key challenges: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells (demonstrated up to 100 million), and modeling how covariates influence expression. This enables more accurate and scalable integration of large transcriptomic atlases.

papers.title: Sphinx: An R package for adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling and functional analysis in spatial omics.
papers.abstract: Spatial omics enables analysis of tissue microenvironmental heterogeneity, but most spatial tools are optimized for transcriptomics and poorly suited to proteomics data. We developed Sphinx, an R package providing a comprehensive workflow for spatial proteomics, including preprocessing, cell annotation, adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling, and functional characterization. Importantly, it introduces an adaptive parameter selection framework guided by spatial statistical metrics and incorporates computational optimizations for large-scale datasets, enabling robust neighborhood modeling. Notab
papers.summary: Sphinx is an R package designed specifically for spatial proteomics data, offering a complete workflow from preprocessing and cell annotation to adaptive spatial neighborhood modeling and functional analysis. It introduces an adaptive parameter selection framework guided by spatial statistical metrics and includes computational optimizations for large-scale datasets, addressing the gap left by tools optimized primarily for spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: SigBridgeR: An R Toolkit for Standardized Identification and Benchmarking of Phenotype-Associated Cell Subpopulations in Single-Cell Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has revolutionized our understanding of cellular heterogeneity, yet linking specific cell subpopulations to clinically relevant phenotypes remains a major challenge. Although multiple computational methods have been developed to integrate bulk transcriptomic and single-cell data for phenotype-associated cell identification, differences in algorithmic strategies, parameter configurations, software implementations, and output formats make it difficult to compare methods fairly, reproduce analyses, and determine which approach is most suitable for a given bi
papers.summary: SigBridgeR is an R toolkit that standardizes the identification and benchmarking of phenotype-associated cell subpopulations by integrating bulk transcriptomic data with single-cell RNA-seq data. It addresses the current fragmentation in the field—where different algorithms, parameters, and output formats make fair comparison and reproducibility difficult—by providing a unified framework for running and evaluating multiple methods. This enables researchers to more reliably determine which approach best links cell subpopulations to clinical phenotypes.

papers.title: Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity and poor clinical outcomes. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the key molecular determinants underlying EMT-associated malignant states remain incompletely defined, and their translation into clinically accessible tools is challenging. In this study, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in HNSCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) i
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data, including single-cell RNA sequencing, to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The authors identify C16orf74 as a regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) with prognostic relevance, linking an understudied gene to EMT-associated malignant states. The work highlights how multimodal integration can nominate clinically relevant biomarkers in a heterogeneous cancer.

papers.title: Gene Expression Nebulas 2.0: an updated resource of gene expression profiles by incorporating more datasets, annotations, and functionalities.
papers.abstract: Gene Expression Nebulas (GEN; https://ngdc.cncb.ac.cn/gen/) is an open-access database that provides standardized transcriptomic profiles and manually curated metadata across diverse species. Compared with the previous release, the updated GEN has expanded in terms of datasets from 323 to 668, samples from 50 500 to 102 679, cells from 15 540 169 to 23 461 252, and species from 30 to 100. GEN 2.0 adds spatial transcriptomics data and disease-associated expression annotations from 82 human bulk RNA-seq datasets spanning 62 disease categories, including distinct subtypes, across 12 disease syste
papers.summary: GEN 2.0 is an updated open-access database of standardized gene expression profiles spanning 668 datasets, over 100,000 samples, and 100 species. The new release adds spatial transcriptomics data and disease-associated expression annotations covering 62 disease categories across 12 disease systems. It provides a substantially expanded, manually curated resource for comparative and disease-focused transcriptomic analyses.

papers.title: Multi-omics characterization of the tumor microenvironment in thyroid cancer with multi-organ metastasis.
papers.abstract: Differentiated thyroid carcinoma (DTC) has one of the most favorable prognoses among all human malignant tumors. However, distant metastases significantly reduce patient survival rates, causing the 5-year survival rate to plummet from over 98% for primary tumors to below 50%. Therefore, elucidating the mechanisms driving DTC metastasis is crucial. This study integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic techniques to analyze patient-derived samples from the primary lesion and multiple metastatic lesions (including lymph node, bone, and brain metastases), constructing high-resolution maps o
papers.summary: This study used single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map the tumor microenvironment of differentiated thyroid cancer across a primary lesion and multiple metastatic sites (lymph node, bone, and brain). The high-resolution atlas reveals how cellular composition and spatial organization of the microenvironment differ between primary tumors and distant metastases, offering insight into mechanisms driving metastasis and potential immunotherapy targets.

papers.title: The CD39/CD73 adenosinergic pathway is increased by proinflammatory states and modified by chemo-radiation in human non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Recent clinical trials show prominent anti-tumor activity of CD73-blocking antibodies in combination with programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) antagonists in a subset of patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), which highlights the need to understand the properties of the CD39/CD73 pathway in human lung malignancies and its modulation by other anti-cancer therapies. To address this, we study the distribution, biological context, spatial heterogeneity, clinical significance, and modulation of CD39/CD73 using multiplexed quantitative immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomic
papers.summary: This study maps the CD39/CD73 adenosinergic pathway in human non-small cell lung cancer using multiplexed immunofluorescence and spatial transcriptomics, showing that proinflammatory states increase pathway expression and that chemo-radiation modifies it. The findings help explain how this immunosuppressive pathway is regulated in lung tumors and may inform combination strategies with CD73-blocking antibodies.

papers.title: Dupilumab modulates type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor-expressing immune cells in eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis.
papers.abstract: Eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (eCRS) is a refractory type 2 inflammatory disease characterized by nasal polyp formation and eosinophilic infiltration. Although dupilumab, an IL-4Rα-blocking antibody, demonstrates clinical efficacy, its cellular mechanisms within nasal polyps remain unclear.
papers.journal: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
papers.summary: This study investigates how dupilumab, an antibody blocking the IL-4 receptor alpha, affects immune cells in nasal polyps of patients with eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis. The work aims to clarify the cellular mechanisms behind the drug's clinical benefit in this type 2 inflammatory disease, focusing on cells expressing the type II IL-4/IL-13 receptor.

papers.title: Novel adenoma-immune phenotypes are associated with risk of metachronous polyps and colorectal cancer in a bowel screening cohort.
papers.abstract: Current British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk.
papers.summary: This study examined immune cell profiles within screen-detected colorectal adenomas to see whether they predict the risk of later (metachronous) polyps and colorectal cancer. It identifies novel adenoma-immune phenotypes linked to metachronous lesion risk, suggesting immune profiling could improve on current BSG guidelines, which misclassify risk in about 40% of patients after polypectomy.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, training a gradient-boosted meta-classifier on the raw scores from ten different inference methods so that method weighting varies by edge rather than being fixed globally. They also introduce a diagnostic typology to characterize why methods disagree. Evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens, this score-level arbitration aims to resolve inter-method conflicts more principledly than picking one method or simple averaging.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with machine learning to build a prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature (PIS) for non-small cell lung cancer, based on epithelial cell-derived genes. The signature stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS patients showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. ADAM12 is identified and validated as a key functional regulator through cell line and mouse experiments.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication from spatial transcriptomics data into three groups: cell-type or single-cell resolution network inference, microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability modeling, and regulatory modulation. It highlights how spatial context enables more biologically grounded communication inference than scRNA-seq alone and provides guidance for selecting methods based on the biological question.

papers.title: A contextual activity score (CAS) for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity across RNA-seq, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Adenosine-to-inosine RNA editing, catalyzed by Adenosine Deaminases Acting on RNA (ADARs), is a widespread modification involved in neural function, immune regulation, and cancer. The Alu Editing Index (AEI) is the standard metric to estimate ADAR activity but requires raw sequencing reads and is poorly suited for single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data. This study aimed to develop an alternative framework for inferring ADAR-associated transcriptional activity from gene expression data across diverse transcriptomic technologies.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: The authors introduce a Contextual Activity Score (CAS) that infers ADAR-associated RNA editing activity directly from gene expression data, bypassing the need for raw sequencing reads required by the standard Alu Editing Index. This makes it applicable to single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, where read-level editing quantification is impractical. The framework thus extends ADAR activity inference to a much broader range of transcriptomic technologies.

papers.title: An integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulatory circuit orchestrated by NUDT21 maintains the proliferation and survival of neuroblastoma.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma (NB) is the most prevalent pediatric solid tumor associated with a poor prognosis. While alternative polyadenylation (APA) is a key post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in many cancers, its role in NB remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study investigates how alternative polyadenylation (APA), a post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism, contributes to neuroblastoma, the most common pediatric solid tumor. The authors identify NUDT21 as a central orchestrator of an integrated transcriptional and post-transcriptional circuit that sustains neuroblastoma cell proliferation and survival, suggesting APA regulation as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis highlights TM4SF4 + epithelial cells and the MMP14-associated signaling program in lung adenocarcinoma pathogenesis and microenvironment remodeling.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression is shaped by aberrant cell-cell and cell-matrix communication within a heterogeneous tumor microenvironment (TME). This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), genome-wide association study, and spatial transcriptomics to identify epithelial subpopulations associated with this crosstalk. Analyzing GSE196303 scRNA-seq data, we resolved 15 epithelial subpopulations. Using scPagwas, the TM4SF4 + subpopulation showed the highest trait-relevance score for LUAD genetic susceptibility (adjusted p < 0.05). BayesPrism deconvolution of TCGA-LUAD da
papers.journal: Journal of cell communication and signaling
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, GWAS, and spatial transcriptomics to dissect how epithelial subpopulations and their signaling interact with the lung adenocarcinoma microenvironment. It identifies a TM4SF4+ epithelial subpopulation with the strongest genetic susceptibility signal for LUAD and highlights an MMP14-associated signaling program implicated in microenvironment remodeling. The work nominates candidate cell states and pathways for further functional and clinical investigation.

papers.title: An ibuprofen-eluting electrospun membrane prevents ureteral fibrosis by dampening macrophage-associated fibroblast activation.
papers.abstract: Ureteral stricture is driven by unresolved inflammation and progressive matrix deposition, yet mechanism-guided local therapies remain limited.
papers.summary: This study develops an electrospun membrane that locally releases ibuprofen to prevent ureteral stricture (scarring) after injury. The authors show that the drug dampens macrophage-driven activation of fibroblasts, reducing fibrosis in a preclinical model. The work suggests a mechanism-guided local therapy for a condition with few targeted treatment options.

papers.title: Decoding pyroptosis at single-cell resolution: heterogeneity, microenvironment remodeling and potential translational insights.
papers.abstract: Pyroptosis, a pro-inflammatory programmed cell death mediated by inflammatory caspases and Gasdermin (GSDM) family proteins, exerts dual roles in host defense and pathological damage. Traditional bulk RNA sequencing (bulk RNA-seq) is limited in capturing single-cell heterogeneity and dissecting intercellular communication, impeding in-depth mechanistic exploration of pyroptosis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these limitations, enabling high-throughput profiling of single-cell transcriptomes and precise characterization of gene expression heter
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell RNA sequencing is being used to study pyroptosis, an inflammatory form of programmed cell death driven by caspases and Gasdermin proteins. The authors argue that scRNA-seq overcomes the limitations of bulk RNA-seq by capturing cell-to-cell heterogeneity and intercellular communication in pyroptotic processes, and they highlight implications for microenvironment remodeling and translational applications.

papers.title: Reanalysis of public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptomes identifies widespread tumor-normal dysregulation and a cross-layer cell-cycle signal in sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC) is a rare malignancy affecting the nasal cavity and paranasal sinuses, with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection identified as a critical etiological factor in a subset of cases. HPV-positive and HPV-negative SNSCC exhibit distinct clinical behaviors, with HPV-positive tumors generally demonstrating better prognosis and treatment response. However, the cellular composition and transcriptomic landscape of SNSCC tumor versus normal tissue remain incompletely characterized. Multi-layer transcriptomic reanalysis of publicly available single-nucleus and bul
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed public bulk and single-nucleus transcriptome datasets to compare tumor and normal tissue in sinonasal squamous cell carcinoma (SNSCC), a rare head-and-neck cancer. The authors report widespread tumor-normal transcriptional dysregulation and identify a cell-cycle signal that appears consistently across bulk and single-nucleus layers, while also contrasting HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors. The work is a secondary analysis that characterizes the cellular composition and transcriptomic landscape of SNSCC rather than generating new experimental data.

papers.title: A conserved EREG + IL1RN + macrophage program defines an inflammation-associated transcriptional state linked to WTAP reprogramming and preterm premature rupture of membranes.
papers.abstract: Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) is a major cause of spontaneous preterm birth, yet the cellular mechanisms linking inflammation to membrane dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic datasets from multiple maternal-fetal interface tissues to construct a comprehensive atlas of inflammatory signaling during early pregnancy. Macrophages emerged as the predominant source of basal inflammatory activity, and secondary clustering identified a conserved EREG + IL1RN + macrophages characterized by elevated inflammatory an
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: By integrating single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic datasets across maternal-fetal interface tissues, the authors built an atlas of inflammatory signaling in early pregnancy and identified a conserved EREG+IL1RN+ macrophage subpopulation as the dominant source of basal inflammation. This inflammatory state appears linked to WTAP-mediated transcriptional reprogramming and to preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM), suggesting a cellular mechanism connecting inflammation to membrane dysfunction.

papers.title: Cross-species single-cell and spatial transcriptomics map the conserved stromal remodeling landscape of inflammatory arthritis.
papers.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a condition characterized by chronic synovial inflammation and joint destruction. However, the precise networks linking cellular activation to stromal-mediated pathology remain poorly defined, hindering the development of targeted therapies.
papers.summary: This study uses cross-species single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map the stromal cell remodeling landscape in inflammatory arthritis, comparing human rheumatoid arthritis with animal models. The authors identify conserved stromal cell states and activation networks that link inflammation to joint destruction, providing a framework for targeted therapeutic development.

papers.title: Residual disease as a therapy-remodeled ecosystem: spatial niches, tumor persistence, and relapse in solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Residual disease comprises the malignant burden that remains after treatment, including low-volume lesions and clinically occult reservoirs. Surviving cells encounter a tissue environment altered by cell death, inflammation, repair, stromal activation, vascular injury, and metabolic stress. These changes can support spatially restricted persistence, but co-localization alone does not establish a protective niche. This narrative review links therapy-associated tissue remodeling to the location and state of residual cells and to the timing of potential relapse-directed intervention. We distingui
papers.summary: This narrative review argues that residual disease after cancer therapy should be viewed as a therapy-remodeled ecosystem rather than simply surviving tumor cells. It links treatment-induced tissue changes—cell death, inflammation, repair, stromal activation, vascular injury, and metabolic stress—to the spatial niches where residual cells persist and to the timing of relapse-directed interventions, while cautioning that co-localization alone does not prove a protective niche.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Integration Reveals Key Genes and Potential Metabolic Mediation Mechanisms in Atopic Dermatitis.
papers.abstract: To integrate expression quantitative trait locus-based Mendelian randomization (eQTL-MR), spatial transcriptomics, summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), mediation MR, and exploratory virtual knockout to prioritize candidate genes and potential metabolic mediation pathways in atopic dermatitis (AD).
papers.summary: This study combines multiple Mendelian randomization approaches (eQTL-MR, SMR, mediation MR) with spatial transcriptomics and virtual knockout to prioritize candidate genes and metabolic pathways for atopic dermatitis. It aims to move beyond correlation by using genetic instruments to infer causal gene expression and metabolite-mediated effects in AD.

papers.title: CD97 Modulates M1-Like Macrophage Activation and Function to Influence the Immune Microenvironment and Tumor Progression in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: CD97 is overexpressed in various cancers, but its function and immunoregulatory role in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the expression, function, and potential regulatory mechanisms of CD97 in TNBC.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of CD97, a protein overexpressed in several cancers, in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The authors examine how CD97 influences M1-like macrophage activation and function, thereby shaping the immune microenvironment and tumor progression. The findings suggest CD97 may serve as an immunoregulatory target in TNBC.

papers.title: Investigating the Expression and Function of PPP2R1A in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multi-Omics Analysis with in vitro Validation.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to diagnose early and to treat effectively. Protein Phosphatase 2A Regulatory Subunit Aα (PPP2R1A), the scaffolding (Aα) subunit of the PP2A holoenzyme, is altered in several cancer types, but its expression pattern, functional significance, and translational relevance in HCC are incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates the expression and functional role of PPP2R1A, a scaffolding subunit of the PP2A phosphatase complex, in hepatocellular carcinoma using multi-omics data combined with in vitro experiments. The authors characterize PPP2R1A expression patterns in HCC and assess its functional significance and potential translational relevance. The work extends existing knowledge of PP2A subunit dysregulation to liver cancer, though the abstract does not report specific findings.

papers.title: Immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor axes in osteoarthritis: microenvironmental control of inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is increasingly recognized as a whole-joint disease shaped by chronic low-grade inflammation, matrix damage, mechanical stress, and failed tissue repair. Beyond the traditional view of cartilage wear, emerging evidence indicates that immune-chondrocyte ligand-receptor (LR) communication plays a central role in translating microenvironmental cues into disease-relevant chondrocyte phenotypes. In this narrative review, we summarize major immune-derived or inflammation-amplified LR axes that regulate OA progression, including cytokine pathways such as IL-1β-IL-1R, TNF-α-TNFR, I
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disease driven by chronic low-grade inflammation, in which ligand-receptor communication between immune cells and chondrocytes translates microenvironmental cues into disease-relevant chondrocyte phenotypes. It catalogs major immune-derived or inflammation-amplified axes—such as IL-1β–IL-1R and TNF-α–TNFR—that regulate inflammation, matrix remodeling, and chondrocyte fate. The review frames these immune-chondrocyte interactions as central to OA progression rather than cartilage wear alone.
